content.value_statement: Daily planning across Lark meetings and tasks can be scattered. This skill gathers both sources and turns them into a concise standup report.
actual_capabilities: Runs lark-cli calendar agenda commands for today or a specified date range.
Runs lark-cli task queries for incomplete tasks assigned to the current user.
Combines calendar events and tasks into one dated standup summary.
Maps RSVP status values into readable meeting status labels.
Sorts events and tasks by time, due date, and completion relevance.
Highlights overlapping meetings and estimated free time from the schedule.
limitations: Requires lark-cli to be installed and authenticated with calendar and task scopes.
Only supports user identity access, not bot or app-only workflows.
Natural-language dates must be converted to ISO 8601 or timestamps before commands run.
Large task histories may need filtering to stay within context limits.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Personal Morning Brief
use_cases.description: Create a same-day view of meetings, pending tasks, conflicts, and free time before work begins.

use_cases.title: Review Team Planning Load
use_cases.description: Summarize assigned tasks and meeting commitments before a standup or weekly planning discussion.

use_cases.title: Check Schedule Risk Before Delivery
use_cases.description: Find overlapping meetings and overdue tasks that could affect a near-term project milestone.

prompt_templates.title: Today Summary
prompt_templates.prompt: Create my Lark standup report for today. Include meetings, incomplete tasks, conflicts, and open time blocks.

prompt_templates.title: Tomorrow Preview
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Lark standup report for tomorrow. Convert the date to the required command format before collecting events and tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Weekly Agenda Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a standup report for this work week. Group meetings by day and list tasks due before the end of the week.

prompt_templates.title: Conflict and Task Risk Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my Lark calendar and tasks for the selected date range. Prioritize schedule conflicts, overdue tasks, and free time for focused work.

output_examples.input: Create my standup report for today.
output_examples.output: A dated report with a meeting table, pending task list, conflict notes, and a short summary of workload.

output_examples.input: Show tomorrow's Lark schedule and unfinished tasks.
output_examples.output: A next-day preview with calendar events in time order, tasks due by tomorrow, and free time estimates.

output_examples.input: Check this week for schedule conflicts and overdue tasks.
output_examples.output: A weekly planning summary that flags overlapping meetings, declined events, overdue work, and tasks without due dates.

best_practices: Authenticate lark-cli before use and confirm the requested calendar and task read scopes.
Use explicit ISO 8601 dates or timestamps for custom date ranges.
Filter tasks by due date when the account has a large task history.
anti_patterns: Do not pass natural-language dates directly to lark-cli date arguments.
Do not request unrelated Lark scopes for a standup report.
Do not include old unbounded task lists without summarizing or filtering them.

faq.question: Does this skill require Lark access?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires lark-cli authentication with calendar and task read permissions for the current user.

faq.question: Can it summarize tomorrow or next week?
faq.answer: Yes. The AI must convert those dates into ISO 8601 values or timestamps before running commands.

faq.question: Does it create or update tasks?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow only reads calendar events and assigned tasks for reporting.

faq.question: Can it detect meeting conflicts?
faq.answer: Yes. It sorts events by start time and flags overlaps where one event ends after the next begins.

faq.question: What happens with declined meetings?
faq.answer: Declined meetings are labeled as declined and excluded from busy time and conflict calculations.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
